name: Oranjestad Centre
tagline: The Dutch colonial capital and its main street
description: The compact centre around Caya Betico Croes, with pastel Dutch colonial facades, the free streetcar looping through it and the cruise terminal on the water. It is the administrative and commercial heart of Aruba and quieter than the hotel strips.
bestFor: Anyone who wants to be in a town rather than a resort
pros: Walkable centre with a free streetcar
Buses to the whole island from here
cons: Busy on cruise days and dead otherwise

name: Palm Beach and Noord
description: The northwestern strip of tall hotels, casinos, restaurants and bars along Palm Beach, with the Noord district behind it holding supermarkets and residential streets. It is the busiest and most commercial part of Aruba and where the nightlife is.
bestFor: Anyone who wants restaurants, bars and a beach on the doorstep
pros: Calm swimming and the pier for snorkelling
Fisherman's Huts for windsurfing at the north end
cons: The most expensive area on Aruba
Traffic on the strip in the evening

name: Eagle Beach
tagline: Low-rise, wide sand and the divi-divi trees
description: The stretch of beach south of Palm Beach, kept low-rise by planning rules, with the two wind-bent divi-divi trees that appear on every Aruba postcard. The beach here is wider and considerably less crowded than the high-rise strip.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the best beach without the high-rise wall behind it
pros: Wider and quieter than Palm Beach
Turtle nesting protected on the sand
Low-rise planning keeps the outlook open
cons: Little to do on foot beyond the beach

name: San Nicolas
tagline: The old refinery town turned mural district
description: Aruba's second town at the southeastern end, built around the Lago refinery that closed and left it struggling, and reinvented over the last decade as a street art district with large murals across its buildings and a carnival tradition of its own.
bestFor: Budget stays and anyone interested in the island's other side
pros: By far the cheapest housing on Aruba
Serious street art across the town
Baby Beach and Rodgers Beach nearby

name: Savaneta
tagline: The old capital and the fish shacks
description: A fishing village on the south coast, Aruba's original capital, with Zeerover at its centre, a fish shack where you order by the pound and eat over the water. It is the most local part of the developed island and considerably cheaper.
bestFor: Anyone wanting local prices and a quiet coast
pros: Much cheaper than the beach strips
